brief.scope: The ladder batch, unit 2 (the ladder driver), the skeptic pass: judge the tests on this ref against the contract in the input file (the driver scope with the owner's ruling, and the plan's unit 2). The tests are landed on this ref, red first: ops/conductor/tests/test_ladder_lever.py and additions to test_instrument_conventions.py, test_land_lever.py and test_laneconf.py. Judge whether they discriminate (stub levers and a stub gh recording argv and producing planted outcomes; the driver locating levers relative to the worktree), whether every guarantee the plan names for unit 2 is pinned (a stage's input never carries the withheld artifact; a landed commit is a descendant of the stage's base; a stage runs the conf's model and effort; the four exit classes; stop and resume by record), whether the ruling's stage shape is pinned (implement per S bucket, audits once per batch, no skeptic on fixed tests), and whether any test would pass against a wrong driver. No implementation exists yet; do not write one.

findings.claim: The stub labels the second author-tests/tests dispatch as tests-fix, but AuditChanges skips that stage and contractually makes the second call fix-tests. A correct driver therefore fails the fixture.

No fixture declares two S buckets or multiple slices, and no assertion checks bucket calibration. A wrong driver that implements once per M slice and audits after every slice passes; only the no-second-skeptic ruling is pinned.
findings.reproduce: git grep -n -E 'slice|batch|bucket|calibrat|minutes|findings per stage' fca7ec01baae79bfbb39b17120cbfc71b45d121b -- ops/conductor/tests/test_ladder_lever.py

findings.claim: The withholding test omits stage 3 (tests-fix), checks no previous-stage record ID in the given proof, and does not tie the recorded proof to dispatched bytes. A driver that leaks implementation into tests-fix, omits previous envelopes, and fabricates proof fields survives.

The edge stubs are under-discriminating: dispatch accepts no --detach, normal records permit omitted waits, land calls are not matched to write-stage record IDs, no push or remote is planted, and gh omits required head/title/body assertions. A wrong driver can skip waits and push, land review records, and open an incomplete PR; a correct push-before-PR driver has no remote available.

Only a requested-model mismatch at tests is planted. No effort mismatch is possible, and model/effort argv are not asserted for every conditional and review stage. A driver that never verifies model.effort_requested survives.
The planted non-descendant is a blob rather than a valid unrelated commit. A wrong driver that merely rejects non-commit object IDs, without checking merge-base ancestry, passes.

Every resume fixture has one ladder record and supplies that record's ID; the helper selects the newest record. A driver that ignores resume's argument and resumes the newest record passes, as does one that never commits each transition.
Every successful invocation runs inside the requested branch's current worktree, which also owns the stubs. A wrong driver that uses cwd instead of resolving the named branch's worktree passes.

The exit test checks membership only for observed paths and plants no invalid envelope, landing abort, wait wall, ledger failure, or crash. A driver returning an out-of-wire exit for those contract-named failures passes.
Every Reauthor case uses ready() with one producer although both flags must affect every cherry-picked commit. A land lever that re-authors or co-authors only the last commit passes.
